## 1. Discovery & Translational Science

* **Indazole-based Spns2 inhibitors identified for S1P pathway modulation** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800620/)
  * Structure-activity relationship profiling identified novel indazole derivatives as potent inhibitors of Spinster homolog 2 (Spns2)-dependent sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) release.

* **Collagen-targeted IL-12 synergizes with doxorubicin in osteosarcoma** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800477/)
  * Preclinical evaluation demonstrated that combining collagen-targeting interleukin-12 (IL-12) with doxorubicin significantly enhances anti-tumor efficacy in osteosarcoma models.

* **Multi-target blood test evaluated for early hepatocellular carcinoma detection** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800682/)
  * Cross-sectional analysis of the prospective ALTUS study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-target blood test for early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma screening.

* **Multi-omics profiling illuminates moxifloxacin neurotoxicity mechanism** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42799811/)
  * Integrative multi-omics analysis links moxifloxacin-associated cognitive impairment to alterations across a proteostasis-translation-neuroimmune signaling axis.

* **Proteomic study maps biomarkers of senescence in aging non-human primates** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42799938/)
  * Plasma and cerebrospinal fluid proteomic profiling in aging rhesus macaques revealed distinct molecular signatures associated with cellular senescence and neuropathology.

* **Translational species differences identified in endothelial vasorelaxation** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800546/)
  * Comparative preclinical evaluation across isolated vascular beds from mice, non-human primates, and humans highlights key species-specific differences in endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation.

* **Cocrystallization technique enhances solubility of hydrophobic flavonoid** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800670/)
  * Tuning surface chemistry through cocrystallization improved the wettability and dissolution properties of a hydrophobic flavonoid drug candidate.

* **Radix Astragali modulates hepatocyte energy metabolism** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800688/)
  * Preclinical investigation showed Radix Astragali exerts hepatoprotective effects by regulating hepatocyte mitochondrial energy metabolism and maintaining oxidative homeostasis.

* **GPCR heteromers highlighted as targets for neuropsychiatric drug discovery** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800225/)
  * Review underscores GPCR heteromers as novel functional targets beyond monomeric receptors to advance drug discovery across neuropsychiatric indications.

* **Shared pathways explored in XDP, SCA36, and ALS/FTD** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42799858/)
  * Comparative analysis of X-linked Dystonia-Parkinsonism and Spinocerebellar Ataxia type 36 through the lens of ALS/FTD models elucidates converging neurodegenerative disease mechanisms.

## 2. Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **Phase 2 trial reports on cultivated oral mucosal epithelial transplantation** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800636/)
  * Phase 2 trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of cultivated oral mucosal epithelial transplantation (COMET) in patients with severe ocular surface disorders.

* **Pooled analysis evaluates second-line TKIs post-immunotherapy in HCC** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800536/)
  * Pooled individual patient-data analysis assessed clinical outcomes of second-line multikinase inhibitors following progression on first-line immunotherapy in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.

## 4. Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves imlunestrant plus abemaciclib in ESR1-mutated breast cancer** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * Approved imlunestrant in combination with abemaciclib for the treatment of ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA grants accelerated approval to camizestrant combination** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * Granted accelerated approval to camizestrant combined with a CDK4/6 inhibitor for patients with ESR1-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA expands Stelara to pediatric ulcerative colitis** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * Approved Stelara (ustekinumab) for the treatment of pediatric patients with ulcerative colitis.

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA adds boxed warning to Injectafer for severe hypophosphatemia** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * Updated labeling for ferric carboxymaltose injection (Injectafer) to include a Boxed Warning detailing the risk of severe low blood phosphate levels (hypophosphatemia).

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA issues safety communication on off-label Kybella use** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * Issued a Drug Safety Communication and updated labeling for Kybella (deoxycholic acid) injection to warn against adverse reactions associated with unapproved uses.

* **FDA approves portfolio of rare disease therapies and label extensions** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * Approved the first drug to treat Alexander disease, a third therapy for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), and a treatment for ataxia in patients with ataxia-telangiectasia.
  * Cleared the first therapy targeting muscle loss in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and approved the first drug indicated for children aged 4–11 with activated PI3K delta syndrome (APDS).
  * Granted approvals for polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia, adult dermatomyositis, pediatric idiopathic nephrotic syndrome (ages ≥2), and neonatal HIV infection.

## 5. Business & Strategy

* **Analysis highlights slow pace of novel drug target discovery post-genome sequencing** [X / @paras_biotech](https://x.com/paras_biotech/status/2104063983766606210)
  * Industry commentary notes that only 312 new drug targets have been validated since 2000 (an 84% cumulative increase), representing an average yield of 12–15 novel targets per year.

* **Commentary examines drivers of rare disease market growth** [X / @paras_biotech](https://x.com/paras_biotech/status/2103947871783645226)
  * Analysis emphasizes that rare disease commercial expansion is primarily driven by active clinical trials, drug approvals, and improved diagnostic reporting that uncover existing undiagnosed populations, rather than true epidemiological incidence growth.

## 6. Public Health & Policy

* **Cohort study correlates visual impairment progression with elevated dementia risk** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42801054/)
  * Observational study identified significant associations between the severity and longitudinal progression of visual impairment and an increased risk of incident dementia.

* **Biobank study identifies exposome risk factors for angle-closure glaucoma** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800676/)
  * Exposome-wide association study using data from the China Kadoorie Biobank mapped environmental and lifestyle risk factors for primary angle-closure glaucoma.

* **Study tracks Hodgkin lymphoma transformation in chemo-naïve CLL** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42800804/)
  * Clinical study evaluated incidence patterns and disease dynamics of Hodgkin lymphoma transformation in chemotherapy-naïve chronic lymphocytic leukemia patients.

**Worth watching:** The simultaneous FDA regulatory moves expanding oral SERDs and novel endocrine combinations (imlunestrant, camizestrant) into ESR1-mutated breast cancer mark a major shift in second-line HR+/HER2- treatment paradigms.

- Biology & Health
    - [Dr. Fung: ‘Cholesterol is barely relevant to Heart Disease’](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R3FtYEk7nc8) -- Physionic
        - The video evaluates Dr. Jason Fung's claim regarding the minimal relevance of blood cholesterol to heart disease, comparing lipid levels against other prospective risk factors.
        - It reviews clinical guidelines and risk assessment tools, including the AHA PREVENT equations and the ACC/AHA dyslipidemia management guidelines.
        - It references clinical trial evidence, such as the IMPROVE-IT trial evaluating ezetimibe added to statin therapy, alongside EAS/EFLM consensus recommendations for quantifying atherogenic lipoproteins.
        - It analyzes observational and meta-analytic data, including 61 prospective studies on blood cholesterol and vascular mortality as well as Danish cohort studies on LDL levels and all-cause mortality.
        - It highlights the relative impact of lipid, inflammatory, and metabolic biomarkers on the age of onset for incident coronary heart disease and lifetime cardiovascular risk.
